name: Gojoseon, Three Kingdoms, Goryeo & Joseon Korea
summary: Maintained remarkable political and cultural continuity on the Korean Peninsula. Goryeo invented the world’s first metal movable-type printing press (Jikji, 1377—decades before Gutenberg) and celadon ceramics, while King Sejong of Joseon personally commissioned the scientific Hangul alphabet in 1443 to bring universal literacy to commoners.
keyFacts: World’s earliest extant metal movable-type book (Jikji, 1377) & Tripitaka Koreana (81,258 woodblocks)
Hangul featural alphabet (1443) & Cheomseongdae (oldest surviving astronomical observatory in Asia)

name: Yayoi, Heian, Shogunates & Modern Japan
summary: From Jōmon cord-marked pottery and Kofun keyhole mounds to the refined Heian court (where Murasaki Shikibu wrote The Tale of Genji, the world’s first psychological novel, c. 1008), followed by samurai shogunates, 250 years of Edo urban peace, the Meiji industrial transformation (1868), and post-WWII technological leadership.
keyFacts: Murasaki Shikibu’s The Tale of Genji (c. 1008 CE) & Hōryū-ji (world’s oldest wooden buildings)
Edo-period ukiyo-e woodblock prints (Hokusai, Hiroshige) and near-universal urban literacy
Meiji Restoration & Shinkansen / high-tech industrial miracle
